title: Non-invasive identification of TKI-resistant NSCLC: a multi-model AI approach for predicting EGFR/TP53 co-mutations.
authors: Li, Jiayi; Xu, Renjie; Wang, Dan; Liang, Zhanlue; Li, Yangqian; Wang, Qinglan; Bi, Lingfeng; Qi, Yawen; Zhou, Yaojie; Li, Weimin
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用CT影像和机器学习预测NSCLC中EGFR/TP53共突变，属于临床影像组学应用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the value of multi-model based on preoperative CT scans in predicting EGFR/TP53 co-mutation status. METHODS: We retrospectively included 2171 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with pre-treatment computed tomography (CT) scans and predicting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene sequencing from West China Hospital between January 2013 and April 2024. The deep-learning model was built for predicting EGFR / tumor protein 53 (TP53) co-occurrence status. The model performance was evaluated by area under the curve (AUC) and Kaplan-Meier analysis. We further compared multi-dimension model with three one-dimension models separately, and we explored the value of combining clinical factors with machine-learning factors. Additionally, we investigated 546 patients with 56-panel next-generation sequencing and low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) to explore the biological mechanisms of radiomics. RESULTS: In our cohort of 2171 patients (1,153 males, 1,018 females; median age 60 years), single-dimensional models were developed using data from 1,055 eligible patients. The multi-dimensional model utilizing a Random Forest classifier achieved superior performance, yielding the highest AUC of 0.843 for predicting EGFR/TP53 co-mutations in the test set. CONCLUSION: The multi-dimensional model demonstrates promising potential for non-invasive prediction of EGFR and TP53 co-mutations, facilitating early and informed clinical decision-making in NSCLC patients at risk of treatment resistance.
abstract_zh: 目的：探讨基于术前CT扫描的多模型在预测EGFR/TP53共突变状态中的价值。方法：我们回顾性纳入了2013年1月至2024年4月期间来自华西医院的2171例非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）患者，这些患者具有治疗前计算机断层扫描（CT）图像及预测性表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）基因测序数据。构建了深度学习模型用于预测EGFR/肿瘤蛋白53（TP53）共发生状态。模型性能通过曲线下面积（AUC）和Kaplan-Meier分析进行评估。我们进一步将多维模型与三个一维模型分别进行比较，并探讨了将临床因素与机器学习因素相结合的价值。此外，我们研究了546例具有56基因panel下一代测序和低剂量计算机断层扫描（LDCT）的患者，以探索影像组学的生物学机制。结果：在我们的2171例患者队列中（男性1,153例，女性1,018例；中位年龄60岁），使用1,055例符合条件的患者数据开发了单维模型。采用随机森林分类器的多维模型表现出优越性能，在测试集中预测EGFR/TP53共突变的AUC最高，为0.843。结论：多维模型在非侵入性预测EGFR和TP53共突变方面展现出巨大潜力，有助于NSCLC患者中面临治疗耐药风险者进行早期且明智的临床决策。
